answer.worked: Triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $C$, and its angle at $B$ is $45^\circ$, so its angle at $A$ is also $45^\circ$. In right triangle $ACN$, $\alpha=180^\circ-90^\circ-45^\circ=45^\circ$. In triangle $CNB$, the angle at $C$ is also $45^\circ$, so $CN=NB=4$. Triangle $ACN$ likewise has equal legs, giving $AN=CN=4$ and $x=4$.

answer.worked: The right angle at $A$ is split into $15^\circ$, $\alpha$ and $15^\circ$. Thus $\alpha=90^\circ-15^\circ-15^\circ=60^\circ$. Since $AP=AQ=5$, triangle $APQ$ is isosceles with vertex angle $60^\circ$; its other two angles are also $60^\circ$. It is equilateral, so $PQ=x=5$.
